text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, fine thanks. I'm Carys.
A: Gemma. Nice to meet you. How are you?
B: Good, thanks. You?
A: Not bad. Two calls down. Where are you calling from?
B: Mold, in Flintshire. North Wales.
A: Oh lovely. We do Haven in North Wales most October half-terms with our Lily. I'm in Wigan.
B: Ah, I can hear it. What do you do?
A: Primary teacher, Year 4. I'm maths lead as well. What about you?
B: Civil engineer. Flood risk and drainage, mostly. Councils bring us the places that keep flooding and I try and stop it.
A: Oh, that's dead interesting. We had a flood at school a couple of years ago, actually. The playground drain backed up and the whole Key Stage 1 bit was under water. The kids thought it was brilliant.
B: They always do. It was probably a blocked gully, or the drain was undersized for the area. A lot of school sites were built before anyone thought about it properly. Then they add a car park, all that hardstanding, and the water's got nowhere to go.
A: That's exactly what happened, they'd just done the car park! You'd have sorted them out.
B: I'd have written them a very long report.
A: Have you got kids?
B: One. Rhys, he's sixteen. Doing his mocks, very relaxed about them, unlike me.
A: Ha. Lily's eleven, starting high school in September. It's just me and her, really. Her dad has her every other weekend.
B: Same here, more or less. Rhys's dad's in Chester, he has him Sundays.
A: Oh, is it? It's hard work, isn't it. I don't know what I'd do without my mum, she does pick-ups on my staff meeting days.
B: Yes. Mine too. More than I'd like, if I'm honest.
A: I worry about that a bit. What happens when they can't, you know.
B: Yeah. I try not to think about it too hard.
A: Sorry, that's gone a bit deep for three minutes. What do you do for fun?
B: I walk. The Clwydian hills most weekends, Moel Famau usually. I got up on Saturday before the cloud came in.
A: Oh, I'd be dead by the top. I do parkrun at Haigh Woodland when Lily's at her dad's, but I'm slow. I'm there for the coffee after, honestly.
B: That's the right reason to go.
A: I've just been telling the lad from Birmingham about pie barms, and he looked at me like I'd said something awful.
B: Pie in a bap? I'd eat that.
A: A bap! Oh, I'll let you off, you're Welsh.
B: Very generous of you.
A: Have you got anything planned this summer?
B: Probably Pembrokeshire. Walking. I've already booked it, I always book ahead.
A: See, you're organised. I still haven't booked Tenerife.
